body:
Global crypto market cap sits at $2.73T after shedding 3.58% over the past 24 hours, a meaningful drawdown that sets a cautious tone heading into the back half of the trading week. The mood is best described as quietly defensive: Fear & Greed slipped from 55 yesterday to 53 today, tipping from Greed back into Neutral territory, and that one-point drift is a decent proxy for the broader session — nothing has broken, but risk appetite is clearly leaking. Volume came in at a hefty figure against a market that is largely drifting lower, which tells you sellers are not panicking but they are consistently present. BTC dominance holding at 60.1% while ETH dominance slides to 10.8% is the most telling structural read of the day: capital is not rotating into alts, it is consolidating at the top of the cap stack.

BTC printed $81,943, up just 0.55% over 24 hours and off 0.08% in the last hour, making it the clear standout in an otherwise red tape. The 7-day figure of -1.15% confirms BTC is essentially rangebound at the upper end of the recent distribution, absorbing selling pressure rather than amplifying it. Volume of $15.85B is respectable and suggests genuine two-way flow rather than a vacuum drift. The level to watch on the upside is obviously the psychological $83K–$84K band; holding above $81K on the downside keeps the constructive thesis intact. A close below $80K on meaningful volume would shift the technical picture materially and would likely accelerate altcoin weakness given how much of the market is already stretched lower on the week.

ETH is the sharper story today, trading at $2,412.94 with a 24-hour loss of 0.75% and a 7-day loss of 3.33% on $6.92B in volume. The ETH/BTC ratio is quietly deteriorating, and with ETH dominance at 10.8%, there is no sign of a rotation catalyst materializing. Among the notable movers lower, DOT is the most aggressive loser at -3.96% on the day and -10.38% on the week, now trading at $1.1 — a level that offers little technical support. ADA follows a similar script at $0.219749, down 1.30% today and -10.74% on the week, which makes it the worst weekly performer in the ZIMR tracked universe. AVAX at $9.74 is down 2.04% and accelerating lower on the week at -4.95%, while LINK at $11.99 gave up 1.40% intraday and has shed 6.76% over 7 days. SOL at $103.72 is down 0.79% today and -5.03% on the week; Fidelity noted SOL shows resilience but flagged areas needing continued observation, which reads as cautious rather than constructive. BNB at $721.99 is the only altcoin posting a 24-hour gain outside of BTC, up 0.23%, though its weekly loss of 3.29% puts that in context.

The macro backdrop is doing no favors. The chip-stock headline — bets losing $52 million in 10 minutes with Wall Street shut, per CoinDesk — is a sharp reminder that derivative crowding in tech-adjacent trades is still a live risk, and crypto has historically had non-zero correlation to semiconductor sentiment during risk-off episodes. On the regulatory and institutional side, the narrative is bifurcating in an interesting way: Goldman, Wells Fargo, and Morgan Stanley are reportedly viewing tokenization as a growth play rather than a threat, while Citrini's widely circulated piece raises the harder question of who actually captures the profit in a tokenized world. Circle is defending USDC economics against stablecoin competitors offering partners a bigger revenue cut, a competitive dynamic that matters for DeFi liquidity conditions. The Cysic bridge exploit — an unauthorized mint of 10 million CYS — is another reminder that smart contract risk remains a live headline risk capable of hitting sentiment at any moment. Tether's strategic investment in AIsa adds to the AI-crypto convergence narrative but is unlikely to move the tape on its own.

The key catalysts to watch from here are threefold. First, whether BTC can hold the $81K level with conviction or begins to test $79K–$80K; a failure there would likely drag DOT, ADA, and AVAX further into uncomfortable territory given their already extended weekly losses. Second, the stablecoin competitive dynamics around USDC deserve monitoring — if Circle loses distribution partnerships, that has second-order effects on DeFi volume and liquidity that could quietly pressure ETH fee revenue and UNI at $7.22. Third, the tokenization institutional narrative is building real momentum, but per the Citrini framing, the market has not yet priced in who wins; any clarity there could be a sharp mover for specific ecosystem tokens. The risk that would most change the picture to the upside is a decisive BTC close above $83K accompanied by a pickup in ETH volume — that combination would signal the rotation trade is finally ready to run. Until then, the path of least resistance in alts remains lower, and the defensive posture BTC dominance is signaling deserves respect.
